definitions.explanation: A layer of sedimentary rock or soil with internally consistent characteristics that distinguishes it from adjacent layers.

examples.japanese: この{崖|がけ}には{何百万年|なんびゃくまんねん}も{前|まえ}の{地層|ちそう}が{見|み}える。
examples.english: Strata from millions of years ago are visible on this cliff.

examples.japanese: {地層|ちそう}を{調|しら}べることで{過去|かこ}の{環境|かんきょう}がわかる。
examples.english: By studying the geological strata, we can understand the environment of the past.

examples.japanese: {化石|かせき}は{特定|とくてい}の{地層|ちそう}から{発見|はっけん}される。
examples.english: Fossils are discovered from specific geological strata.

notes:
USAGE: {地層|ちそう} is a technical term used in geology and earth science to describe layers of rock and sediment.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{地層|ちそう}を{調|しら}べる (to examine strata)
・{地層|ちそう}が{堆積|たいせき}する (strata accumulate)
・{地層|ちそう}の{断面|だんめん} (cross-section of strata)
・{地層|ちそう}{調査|ちょうさ} (geological survey)

GEOLOGICAL TERMS:
・{堆積岩|たいせきがん} - sedimentary rock
・{化石|かせき} - fossil
・{断層|だんそう} - fault
・{褶曲|しゅうきょく} - fold (geological)

STRATIGRAPHY: {地層|ちそう}の{年代|ねんだい}{測定|そくてい} (dating of strata) uses methods like radiocarbon dating and fossil correlation to determine the age of rock layers.
